parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **globalisation**?
choices: Investment by a firm in one country in productive assets such as factories or businesses in another country
The reduction or removal of barriers to international trade such as tariffs and quotas
The growing integration and interdependence of the world's economies through trade, investment, people and information
A firm that has its headquarters in one country and production or service operations in at least one other country

rows.answer:
Correct option: **C** (The growing integration and interdependence of the world's economies through trade, investment, people and information)
A: incorrect, that is the meaning of foreign direct investment (FDI)
B: incorrect, that is the meaning of trade liberalisation
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of multinational corporation (MNC)

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **free trade**?
choices: When a country can produce more of a good than another country using the same resources
International trade that takes place without barriers such as tariffs or quotas
The exchange of goods and services between countries
When a country can produce a good at a lower opportunity cost than another country

rows.answer:
Correct option: **B** (International trade that takes place without barriers such as tariffs or quotas)
A: incorrect, that is the meaning of absolute advantage
C: incorrect, that is the meaning of international trade
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of comparative advantage

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **international trade**?
choices: The exchange of goods and services between countries
Goods and services produced in one country and sold to buyers in other countries
When countries concentrate on producing the goods and services they are best at producing, and trade for others
When a country can produce a good at a lower opportunity cost than another country

rows.answer:
Correct option: **A** (The exchange of goods and services between countries)
B: incorrect, that is the meaning of exports
C: incorrect, that is the meaning of specialisation (between countries)
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of comparative advantage

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **specialisation (between countries)**?
choices: When a country can produce a good at a lower opportunity cost than another country

When countries concentrate on producing the goods and services they are best at producing, and trade for others
When a country can produce more of a good than another country using the same resources

rows.answer:
Correct option: **C** (When countries concentrate on producing the goods and services they are best at producing, and trade for others)
A: incorrect, that is the meaning of comparative advantage
B: incorrect, that is the meaning of exports
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of absolute advantage

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **protectionism**?
choices: The use of barriers to trade to protect domestic firms from foreign competition
A tax placed on imported goods
A new domestic industry that is not yet able to compete with established foreign firms
Selling goods abroad at a price below their cost of production

rows.answer:
Correct option: **A** (The use of barriers to trade to protect domestic firms from foreign competition)
B: incorrect, that is the meaning of tariff
C: incorrect, that is the meaning of infant industry
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of dumping

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **tariff**?
choices: A physical limit on the quantity of a good that can be imported
A group of countries that remove trade barriers between themselves but each keeps its own barriers against non-members
A new domestic industry that is not yet able to compete with established foreign firms
A tax placed on imported goods

rows.answer:
Correct option: **D** (A tax placed on imported goods)
A: incorrect, that is the meaning of quota
B: incorrect, that is the meaning of free trade area
C: incorrect, that is the meaning of infant industry

A new domestic industry that is not yet able to compete with established foreign firms
A physical limit on the quantity of a good that can be imported

rows.answer:
Correct option: **D** (A physical limit on the quantity of a good that can be imported)
A: incorrect, that is the meaning of World Trade Organization (WTO)
B: incorrect, that is the meaning of tariff
C: incorrect, that is the meaning of infant industry

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **exchange rate**?
choices: An exchange rate determined by market forces of demand for and supply of the currency
The value of a currency expressed as the amount of a different currency it can be swapped for
A rise in the value of a currency against another currency in a floating exchange rate system
A fall in the value of a currency against another currency in a floating exchange rate system

rows.answer:
Correct option: **B** (The value of a currency expressed as the amount of a different currency it can be swapped for)
A: incorrect, that is the meaning of floating exchange rate
C: incorrect, that is the meaning of appreciation
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of depreciation

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **appreciation**?
choices: A fall in the value of a currency against another currency in a floating exchange rate system
An exchange rate set by the government or central bank at a particular value against another currency
An exchange rate determined by market forces of demand for and supply of the currency
A rise in the value of a currency against another currency in a floating exchange rate system

rows.answer:
Correct option: **D** (A rise in the value of a currency against another currency in a floating exchange rate system)
A: incorrect, that is the meaning of depreciation
B: incorrect, that is the meaning of fixed exchange rate
C: incorrect, that is the meaning of floating exchange rate

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **depreciation**?
choices: An exchange rate determined by market forces of demand for and supply of the currency
The value of a currency expressed as the amount of a different currency it can be swapped for
A fall in the value of a currency against another currency in a floating exchange rate system
Holdings of foreign currencies by a central bank used to influence the exchange rate

rows.answer:
Correct option: **C** (A fall in the value of a currency against another currency in a floating exchange rate system)
A: incorrect, that is the meaning of floating exchange rate
B: incorrect, that is the meaning of exchange rate
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of foreign currency reserves

parts.text:
The rupee has depreciated by 9% against the US dollar over the past year.

Explain one likely effect of the depreciation on firms that import raw materials.

rows.answer:
Award 1 mark for identifying a relevant point, 1 mark for developing it and 1 mark for applying it to the context.

Example:
- Costs rise (1) because more rupee are needed to buy the same amount of raw materials priced in dollars (1), so importing firms' profits fall or they raise prices after the 9% depreciation (1)
rows.notes: Accept any other valid explanation. Answers with no reference to the context cannot gain the third mark.
